core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Haroun corresponds to the Arabic form هارون (Qur'anic proper name; هَارُون (Hārūn)). Its core sense is aaron, brother of moses, prophet. Haroun is an alternative transliteration of Arabic هَارُون (Hārūn), the Qur'anic form of the prophet Aaron. The source gloss 'The Successor' and the claim that it means 'the just ruler' are unsupported; the name is a proper name. Same name as haroon and harun.

faq.q: What is the origin of Haroun?
faq.a: Haroun is associated with Arabic. Haroun is an alternative transliteration of Arabic هَارُون (Hārūn), the Qur'anic form of the prophet Aaron. The source gloss 'The Successor' and the claim that it means 'the just ruler' are unsupported; the name is a proper name. Same name as haroon and harun.
Yes — the underlying form هارون is Arabic.
Haroun can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Haroun should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. True

faq.q: What does Haroun mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Haroun is rendered ہارون and carries the sense ہارون، موسیٰ کے بھائی، نبی.

faq.q: What does Haroun mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Haroun is rendered هارون and carries the sense هارون، برادر موسی، پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-roun. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Haroun?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Haroun, haroun. Script forms are هارون, ہارون, हारून.

faq.q: Is Haroun a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
